WILLIAMSON COUNTIES                                  §       ADMINISTRATIVE HEARINGS


                 BRIEF FOLLOWING HEARING ON THE MERITS OF
              INTERVENORS JEFFREY H. SCRIBNER, SUSAN SCRIBNER,
                     MICKEY CHANCE AND JIMMY CHANCE

       COMES NOW, Jeffrey H. Scribner, Susan Scribner, Mickey Chance and Jimmy Chance,

Party 728, hereinafter referred to as the (“Scribner and Chance Intervenors”) and file this their

Brief following the Hearing on the Merits and would respectfully show the ALJ’s as follows:

       1. The Applicants presented evidence by and through direct testimony and cross

            examination of the Panel that Route 894 is the Best Meets Route. The Applicants

            utilized a breakdown of the various routes by corridors—North, South and 3 different

            Central corridors.

       2. All witnesses testified, even those proposing the North Corridor, that the North

            Corridor is longer, costs more and crosses more habitable structures.

       3.   The Scribner and Chance Intervenors are both affected by Link U8 which is part of the

            Northern corridor set of routes.
 4. The routes on the Northern corridor were included well after the original application

   was filed which clearly indicates that the Northern corridor routes were not part of the

   group of routes and links that were to be analyzed as part of this transmission line case.

   Additionally, those folks on the various Northern corridor links did not receive

   sufficient and appropriate notice.

5. The Applicants failed to include two additional habitable structures on Route 392,

   which is on the North Corridor. Jeff and Susan Scribner provided testimony and

   photographs of two homes they have built on their property affected by Link U8. Once

   you include the Scribner homes the total number of habitable structures on Route 392

   increases to 138. That is 52 more habitable structures than Route 894 and 42 more than

   Route 487, the Route proposed by PUC representative Poole. Some testified and stated

   that only 40 or 50 more habitable structures is an “insignificant number” but I doubt

   that those 40 or 50 people believe that to be insignificant.

6. The Northern corridor routes, including Route 392 which has been suggested by several

   intervenors, specifically the Solana intervenors and Brady Creek/Wulff Bluff

   intervenors, is expected to cross the Colorado River at Link U3. The ALJ’s heard from

   more than one Oncor panel member as well as PUC representative Poole, that Links

   U2 and U3 would cross the Colorado River in an area that has been designated by the

   Texas Parks and Wildlife as an Ecologically Significant Stream Segment (“ESSS”).

7. In addition to the issue of ESSS designated area, several intervenors testified that there

   was a significant concern with having two major power lines close together crossing a

   location of a major river, such as the Colorado, that is susceptible to major flooding,

   which we all know has been an issue in the last couple of years. This creates a major
    concern of a simultaneous electrical transmission failure. That would be the exact

   situation in crossing the Colorado in Link U3 versus the other central corridors, which

   have been proposed as the best meets route by both the PUC, via Route 487 and Oncor,

   via Link 894. Both Oncor and the PUC suggest crossing the Colorado River in an area

   that has an existing compatible corridor of four pipelines. The testimony clearly

   establishes that there is a significant advantage to this; it would consolidate the

   disturbance by reducing fragmentation of the riparian corridor in this area of the

   Colorado River.

8. While the Scribner and Chance Intervenors are sympathetic to those intervenors on the

   Central Corridors, when measuring the statutory criteria in holistic manner, the only

   routes that can be utilized are those in the Central Corridor. The North Corridor,

   including Route 392, simply makes no sense. It is longer, more expensive, affects 60%

   more habitable structures, crosses a designated ecologically significant stream segment

   (an “ESSS”) and creates a significant threat of a simultaneous failure of two (2) major

   transmission lines. You can not simply look at the one item of crossing the Colorado

   River in a bubble; you must look at the entire route measuring it against all 36 criteria.

   And, when you do that, Route 392 fails.

9. The Scribner and Chance Intervenors respectfully request the ALJ’s to recommend

   either Route 894, the Applicants proposed route, or 487, the PUC’s proposed route.

   These are routes presented and proposed by unbiased parties—not retained by any

   intervenor—and clearly take into account all statutory criteria in a holistic manner.
       Respectfully submitted,
